name: ColdPlasma
description: Cold plasma model: electron-fluid current coupled with Maxwell's equations via a cold-plasma Ohm's law.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Cold-plasma current:

1n₀ ∂𝐣∂t = 1ε 𝐄 + 1ε n₀ 𝐣 × 𝐁₀

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²ε 𝐣

where (n₀, 𝐁₀) denotes an inhomogeneous background.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a fluid electromagnetic model for a cold plasma response. The

electron fluid is represented only through its current, so thermal pressure and kinetic velocity-space effects are omitted. It is useful as a reduced model between vacuum Maxwell and fully kinetic Vlasov-Maxwell dynamics.
normalizationHtml:
Velocities are normalized with the speed of light and the fields satisfy

v̂ = c,   Ê = c B̂.

The dimensionless plasma parameters are the cold-species α = \hatΩₚ/\hatΩc and ε = 1/(\hatΩct̂).
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.maxwell_weak_ampere.MaxwellWeakAmpere
  2. struphy.propagators.ohm_cold.OhmCold
  3. struphy.propagators.jxb_cold.JxBCold
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Electric field energy: electric_energy
  • Magnetic field energy: magnetic_energy
  • Cold-current energy: kinetic_energy
  • Total energy: total_energy
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • cold-plasma wave propagation studies
  • electromagnetic benchmarks with a fluid current response
  • regimes where thermal pressure can be neglected
  • algorithm verification for Maxwell plus current coupling
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • finite-temperature or pressure-driven plasma dynamics
  • kinetic resonances or velocity-space instabilities
  • multi-species hybrid or fully kinetic problems
  • collisional closures beyond the built-in cold-plasma approximation
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a cold-plasma model: 

from struphy.models import ColdPlasma

model = ColdPlasma()
model.em_fields.e_field
model.em_fields.b_field
model.electrons.current

name: HasegawaWakatani
description: Hasegawa-Wakatani equations in 2D for drift-wave turbulence.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Density equation:

∂n∂t = C (φ - n) - [φ, n] - κ   ∂y φ + ν   ∇²ᴺ n

Vorticity equation:

∂ω∂t = C (φ - n) - [φ, ω] + ν   ∇²ᴺ ω

Potential equation:

Δ φ = ω

where [φ, n] = ∂ₓ φ ∂y n - ∂y φ ∂ₓ n, C = C(x, y) and κ and ν are constants (at the moment only N=1 is available).
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a reduced 2D drift-wave turbulence model. The electrostatic

potential is recovered from the vorticity at each step, and the coupled density-vorticity dynamics capture resistive drift-wave behavior without resolving full kinetic physics.
normalizationHtml:
The electrostatic potential is scaled by the thermal-speed unit,

û = \hat vₜₕ,   \hatφ = û x̂.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.poisson_solve.PoissonSolve
  2. struphy.propagators.hasegawa_wakatani_step.HasegawaWakataniStep
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • No default scalar diagnostics are defined by this model.
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • 2D resistive drift-wave turbulence studies
  • reduced electrostatic edge-plasma benchmarks
  • testing Poisson-coupled advection-diffusion solvers
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • three-dimensional electromagnetic turbulence
  • full kinetic Landau or cyclotron physics
  • multi-species warm-fluid closures beyond the reduced HW system
  • self-consistent magnetic-field evolution
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a Hasegawa-Wakatani model: 

from struphy.models import HasegawaWakatani

model = HasegawaWakatani()
model.em_fields.phi
model.plasma.density
model.plasma.vorticity

name: IncompressibleNavierStokesSPH
description: Incompressible Navier-Stokes equations discretized with smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH).
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Incompressible Navier-Stokes:

ρ (∂ₜ 𝐮 + 𝐮 · ∇ 𝐮) = -∇ p - ∇ · σ
∇ · 𝐮 = 0 .

where σ is the viscous stress tensor.

The viscous stress tensor for a Newtonian fluid is given by:

σ = -μ ( ∇ 𝐮 + (∇ 𝐮)ᵀ - 23 (∇ · 𝐮) 𝐈 )

where μ is the dynamic (shear) viscosity and 𝐈 is the identity tensor.
longDescriptionHtml: IncompressibleNavierStokesSPH is the particle-based SPH fluid model...
normalizationHtml:
The characteristic speed is thermal:

û = \hat vₜₕ.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_eta.PushEta
  2. struphy.propagators.push_vxb.PushVxB (if with_B0 is True)
  3. struphy.propagators.push_vin_viscous_potential.PushVinViscousPotential (if with_viscosity is True)
  4. struphy.propagators.poisson_solve.PoissonSolve
  5. struphy.propagators.push_vin_efield.PushVinEfield
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • SPH kinetic energy: en_kin
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • SPH verification with pressure and viscosity
  • meshfree compressible-fluid experiments
  • testing particle-based viscosity and pressure pushers
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • FEEC grid-based fluid or MHD formulations
  • entropy-resolved thermodynamic evolution
  • kinetic plasma physics
  • studies that require exact field-based conservation structures
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize the viscous Euler SPH model: 

from struphy.models import ViscousEulerSPH

model = ViscousEulerSPH()
model.euler_fluid.var

name: LinearExtendedMHDuniform
description: Linear extended MHD with zero-flow equilibrium, for uniform background conditions only.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

Momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀

Pressure:

∂p̃∂t + 53 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

Induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × ( Ũ × 𝐁₀ - 1ε ∇ × B̃ρ₀ × 𝐁₀ ) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearExtendedMHDuniform extends the linear MHD model with Hall

dynamics for a uniform equilibrium. It is targeted at wave propagation and mode studies where the equilibrium is simple but finite Hall corrections are important.
normalizationHtml:
All velocities are normalized by the Alfvén speed,

Û = \hat vA,

and Hall effects enter through ε = 1/(\hatΩct̂).
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.shear_alfven_b1.ShearAlfvenB1
  2. struphy.propagators.hall.Hall
  3. struphy.propagators.magnetosonic_uniform.MagnetosonicUniform
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Flow kinetic energy: en_U
  • Thermal pressure energy: en_p
  • Magnetic perturbation energy: en_B
  • Background pressure energy: en_p_eq
  • Background magnetic energy: en_B_eq
  • Total magnetic energy: en_B_tot
  • Total perturbation energy: en_tot
  • Magnetic helicity-like invariant: helicity
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • linear Hall-MHD wave studies
  • uniform-equilibrium benchmarks for extended MHD
  • comparison against ideal-MHD dispersion in the Hall-corrected regime
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • nonlinear extended-MHD turbulence
  • non-uniform equilibrium configurations
  • kinetic ion/electron effects beyond the Hall correction
  • dissipation-dominated problems with explicit viscosity or resistivity
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a linear extended-MHD model: 

from struphy.models import LinearExtendedMHDuniform

model = LinearExtendedMHDuniform()
model.em_fields.b_field
model.mhd.density
model.mhd.velocity
model.mhd.pressure

name: LinearMHD
description: Linear ideal MHD with zero-flow equilibrium for magnetohydrodynamic wave propagation.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity (mass conservation):

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

Momentum (Lorentz force):

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + (∇ × 𝐁₀) × B̃

Energy (adiabatic process):

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

Induction (Faraday's law):

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model simulates small-amplitude perturbations in a magnetized plasma with a static

equilibrium magnetic field 𝐁₀ and zero background flow. The model solves the linearized ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations, which couple fluid dynamics (density, velocity, pressure) with magnetic field evolution.

The linear MHD system supports three wave families:

  • Alfvén waves: incompressible shear waves propagating along 𝐁₀
  • Fast magnetosonic waves: compressible waves with phase velocity above the Alfvén speed
  • Slow magnetosonic waves: compressible waves with phase velocity below the Alfvén speed

All evolved quantities are perturbations around a stationary equilibrium:

  • ρ̃ - density perturbation
  • Ũ - velocity perturbation
  • p̃ - pressure perturbation
  • B̃ - magnetic field perturbation

The corresponding equilibrium quantities are:

  • ρ₀ - background density
  • p₀ - background pressure
  • 𝐁₀ - background magnetic field
normalizationHtml:
All velocities are normalized by the Alfvén velocity:

Û = v̂A = B̂₀√(μ₀ ρ₀)

The model therefore uses the Alfvén velocity as its characteristic speed scale.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.shear_alfven_propagator.ShearAlfvenPropagator
  2. struphy.propagators.magnetosonic.Magnetosonic
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy (perturbation): EU = 1⁄2 ∫ ρ₀ |Ũ|²   dV
  • Magnetic energy (perturbation): EB = 1⁄2 ∫ |B̃|²⁄μ₀   dV
  • Internal energy (perturbation): Eₚ = ∫ p̃⁄γ - 1   dV with γ = 5/3
  • Total perturbed energy: Eₜₒₜ = EU + EB + Eₚ
  • Equilibrium magnetic energy: EB0 = 1⁄2 ∫ |𝐁₀|²⁄μ₀   dV
  • Equilibrium internal energy: Eₚ₀ = ∫ p₀⁄γ - 1   dV
  • Total magnetic energy: EB,tot = 1⁄2 ∫ |𝐁₀ + B̃|²⁄μ₀   dV
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for studying linear wave propagation in a static magnetized plasma,

including Alfvén and magnetosonic dynamics around a prescribed equilibrium.

Typical use cases include:

  • verification of linear MHD wave dispersion and mode structure
  • perturbative studies around static equilibria
  • benchmark problems for ideal-MHD field-fluid coupling
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • nonlinear MHD dynamics with finite-amplitude perturbations
  • equilibria with non-zero background flow
  • dissipative effects such as resistivity or viscosity
  • kinetic or particle-field effects beyond the fluid MHD description
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a linear MHD model: 

from struphy.models import LinearMHD

model = LinearMHD()

# Access fields
model.em_fields.b_field
model.mhd.density
model.mhd.velocity
model.mhd.pressure

# Access tracked scalar quantities
model.scalars["en_U"]
model.scalars["en_B"]
model.scalars["en_p"]

name: Poisson
description: Weak discretization of Poisson's equation with a diffusion matrix, stabilization and an optional time-dependent right-hand side.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Find φ ∈ H¹ such that

-∇ · D₀(𝐱) ∇ φ + n₀(𝐱) φ = ρ(t, 𝐱)

where n₀, ρ(t) : Ω → ℝ are real-valued functions, ρ(t) is parametrized by time t, and D₀ : Ω → ℝ3 × 3 is a positive matrix. Boundary terms from integration by parts are assumed to vanish.
longDescriptionHtml:
Poisson is the standalone elliptic field-solve model used for weak

diffusion/Poisson problems. It is also the building block reused by other models for initial electrostatic solves.
normalizationHtml:
The coefficient scaling is

D̂ = n̂ / x̂²,   \hatρ = n̂.

No dedicated velocity normalization is used.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.time_dependent_source.TimeDependentSource (if with_t_dep_source is True)
  2. struphy.propagators.poisson_solve.PoissonSolve
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • No default scalar diagnostics are defined by this model.
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • elliptic benchmark problems
  • electrostatic field solves with prescribed source terms
  • testing weak Poisson discretizations and boundary handling
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • hyperbolic time-dependent wave propagation
  • self-consistent kinetic plasma evolution on its own
  • magnetic-field dynamics or full Maxwell coupling
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a Poisson model: 

from struphy.models import Poisson

model = Poisson()
model.em_fields.phi
model.em_fields.source

name: PressureLessSPH
description: Particle discretization of pressureless Euler flow with external forcing.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) = 𝐅

where 𝐅 is an external force.
longDescriptionHtml:
PressureLessSPH is a meshfree particle model for a pressureless fluid.

It is primarily useful as a simple SPH benchmark or as a reduced particle transport model in a prescribed force field or potential.
normalizationHtml:
Velocity and field normalizations:

û = 1 m/s,    F̂ = mn̂ût̂ .
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_eta.PushEta
  2. struphy.propagators.push_vin_efield.PushVinEfield
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • SPH kinetic energy: en_kin
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • meshfree pressureless-flow benchmarks
  • straight-line particle transport with external forcing
  • testing SPH particle loading and diagnostics
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • compressible fluids with pressure forces
  • FEEC-based grid discretizations
  • electromagnetic plasma dynamics
  • viscous or thermal closures
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a pressureless SPH model: 

from struphy.models import PressureLessSPH

model = PressureLessSPH()
model.cold_fluid.var

name: ShearAlfven
description: Shear-Alfvén part of LinearMHD with zero-flow equilibrium.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀

Induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
ShearAlfven is the incompressible magnetic-tension subsystem extracted

from linear MHD. It is useful when one wants to isolate Alfvénic propagation from the full linear MHD model.
normalizationHtml:
All velocities are normalized by the Alfvén speed,

Û = \hat vA.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.shear_alfven_propagator.ShearAlfvenPropagator
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Perturbed kinetic energy: en_U
  • Perturbed magnetic energy: en_B
  • Background magnetic energy: en_B_eq
  • Total magnetic energy including background: en_B_tot
  • Perturbation total energy: en_tot
  • Total energy including background contribution: en_tot2
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • isolated shear-Alfvén wave propagation
  • verification of the ShearAlfven propagator
  • reduced linear-MHD studies without compressibility
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • magnetosonic or compressible wave physics
  • nonlinear MHD dynamics
  • kinetic particle coupling
  • resistive, viscous, or Hall-MHD effects
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a shear-Alfvén model: 

from struphy.models import ShearAlfven

model = ShearAlfven()
model.em_fields.b_field
model.mhd.velocity

name: TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy
description: Linearized, quasi-neutral two-fluid model with zero electron inertia.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Ion momentum:

∂𝐮∂t = -∇ φ + 𝐮 × 𝐁₀ε + ν Δ 𝐮 + 𝐟

Electron momentum:

0 = ∇ φ - 𝐮ₑ × 𝐁₀ε + νₑ Δ 𝐮ₑ + 𝐟ₑ

Quasi-neutrality constraint:

∇ · (𝐮 - 𝐮ₑ) = 0

where 𝐁₀ is a static magnetic field and 𝐟, 𝐟ₑ are given forcing terms.
longDescriptionHtml:
TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy is a reduced linear two-fluid benchmark with

zero electron inertia. It is meant for studying the quasi-neutral solve and the coupled ion/electron velocity response in a simplified setting.

References

[1] Juan Vicente Gutiérrez-Santacreu, Omar Maj, Marco Restelli: Finite element discretization of a Stokes-like model arising in plasma physics, Journal of Computational Physics 2018.
normalizationHtml:
Thermal-speed scaling is used:

û = \hat vₜₕ,   e\hatφ = m \hat vₜₕ².
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.two_fluid_quasi_neutral_full.TwoFluidQuasiNeutralFull
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • No default scalar diagnostics are defined by this model.
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • linear quasi-neutral two-fluid benchmarks
  • Stokes-like plasma model verification
  • testing coupled velocity-potential FEEC solvers
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • nonlinear two-fluid dynamics
  • finite electron inertia effects
  • kinetic phase-space phenomena
  • self-consistent electromagnetic wave propagation
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize the quasi-neutral toy model: 

from struphy.models import TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy

model = TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy()
model.em_fields.phi
model.ions.u
model.electrons.u

name: VariationalBarotropicFluid
description: Barotropic fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ))∂ ρ = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ρ/2.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the simplest variational compressible-fluid model in Struphy.

It keeps only density and velocity and uses a barotropic closure rather than a separate entropy or pressure evolution equation.
normalizationHtml:
The reference flow speed is the Alfvén speed and the internal energy is

scaled with density:

û = \hat vA,   𝒰̂=\hatρ/2.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy: kinetic_energy
  • Thermodynamic energy: thermo_energy
  • Total energy: total_energy
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • barotropic compressible-flow benchmarks
  • testing variational density and momentum propagators
  • reduced fluid studies without entropy evolution
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • non-barotropic thermodynamics
  • magnetic-field dynamics
  • viscous or resistive effects
  • kinetic plasma phenomena
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a variational barotropic-fluid model: 

from struphy.models import VariationalBarotropicFluid

model = VariationalBarotropicFluid()
model.fluid.density
model.fluid.velocity

name: VariationalCompressibleFluid
description: Fully compressible fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ ρ + s ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ s = 0

Entropy:

∂ₜ s + ∇ · (s 𝐮) = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ργ-1 \exp(s / ρ).
longDescriptionHtml:
VariationalCompressibleFluid is the entropy-based compressible fluid

model in the variational family. It is the natural non-magnetic counterpart to the full variational MHD models.
normalizationHtml:
The model uses Alfvén-speed scaling for the flow variables together

with separate units for internal energy and entropy:

û = \hat vA,   𝒰̂=K,   ŝ=\hatρ Cᵥ.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
  3. struphy.propagators.variational_entropy_evolve.VariationalEntropyEvolve
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy: en_U
  • Thermodynamic energy: en_thermo
  • Total energy: en_tot
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • compressible fluid benchmarks with entropy transport
  • testing the variational fluid propagator stack
  • non-magnetic hydrodynamics with conservative thermodynamics
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • magnetic-field evolution or MHD coupling
  • pressureless or barotropic-only reductions
  • kinetic or particle-based transport physics
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a variational compressible-fluid model: 

from struphy.models import VariationalCompressibleFluid

model = VariationalCompressibleFluid()
model.fluid.density
model.fluid.velocity
model.fluid.entropy

name: VariationalPressurelessFluid
description: Pressure-less fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the pressureless limit of the variational fluid hierarchy. It

is intended as a reduced benchmark and as a simple transport model with conservative density and momentum updates.
normalizationHtml:
The flow speed is normalized with the Alfvén speed:

û = \hat vA.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy: kinetic_energy
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • pressureless compressible benchmarks
  • testing the minimal variational fluid update chain
  • reduced transport problems without thermodynamics
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • pressure- or entropy-driven flow
  • magnetic-field coupling
  • viscous/resistive dissipation
  • kinetic particle physics
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a pressureless variational-fluid model: 

from struphy.models import VariationalPressurelessFluid

model = VariationalPressurelessFluid()
model.fluid.density
model.fluid.velocity

name: ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD
description: Delta-f visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ) + ∇ · ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ⊗ ũ ) + 1γ - 1 ∇ p̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ + B̃ × ∇ × B̃ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Pressure:

∂ₜ p̃ + ũ · ∇ (p̃ + p₀) + γ (p̃ + p₀) ∇ · ũ = 1γ - 1 ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ ũ|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × B̃|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × ( (B̃ + 𝐁₀) × ũ ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD is the dissipative perturbative MHD model using

pressure as thermodynamic variable. It is intended for departures from a background equilibrium that are not strictly linear but still naturally formulated as perturbations.
normalizationHtml:
The velocity scale is Alfvénic:

û = \hat vA.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
  3. struphy.propagators.variational_pb_evolve.VariationalPBEvolve
  4. struphy.propagators.variational_viscosity.VariationalViscosity (if with_viscosity is True)
  5. struphy.propagators.variational_resistivity.VariationalResistivity (if with_resistivity is True)
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy: en_U
  • Thermal energies: en_thermo, en_thermo_l1
  • Magnetic energies: en_mag_1, en_mag_2, en_mag_l1
  • Total energies: en_tot, en_tot_l1
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:

name: ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD_with_q
description: Delta-f visco-resistive MHD equations, with the q variable (square root of the pressure), discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · (ρ₀ ũ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ₀ ũ) + 2 q₀γ - 1 ∇ q̃ + 2 q̃γ - 1 ∇ q₀ + 2 q̃γ - 1 ∇ q̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Energy-like variable:

∂ₜ q̃ + ∇ · ( (q₀ + q̃) ũ ) + ( γ2 - 1 ) (q₀ + q̃) ∇ · ũ = 0

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × ( (𝐁₀ + B̃) × ũ ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is the delta f dissipative MHD formulation in the

q-variable representation. It is aimed at perturbative nonlinear MHD studies where the q-formulation is preferred numerically.
normalizationHtml:
The model uses Alfvén-speed normalization:

û = \hat vA.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
  3. struphy.propagators.variational_qb_evolve.VariationalQBEvolve
  4. struphy.propagators.variational_viscosity.VariationalViscosity (if with_viscosity is True)
  5. struphy.propagators.variational_resistivity.VariationalResistivity (if with_resistivity is True)

  • Kinetic energy: en_U
  • Magnetic energies: en_mag_1, en_mag_2

  • Total energy: en_tot

name: ViscoResistiveLinearMHD
description: Linear visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · (ρ₀ ũ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ₀ ũ) + 1γ - 1 ∇ p̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × (𝐁₀ × ũ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the linear dissipative MHD model with pressure as primitive

thermodynamic variable. It is intended for small-amplitude perturbations around an equilibrium while retaining explicit viscosity and resistivity.
normalizationHtml:
The characteristic velocity is the Alfvén speed,

discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_pb_evolve.VariationalPBEvolve
  3. struphy.propagators.variational_viscosity.VariationalViscosity (if with_viscosity is True)

name: ViscoResistiveMHD
description: Full (non-linear) visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ ρ + s ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ s + 𝐁 × ∇ × 𝐁 - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ 𝐮 ) = 0

Entropy:

∂ₜ s + ∇ · (s 𝐮) = 1T ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ 𝐮|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × 𝐁|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ 𝐁 + ∇ × (𝐁 × 𝐮) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ργ-1 \exp(s / ρ), and μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscoResistiveMHD is the full nonlinear dissipative MHD model in the

entropy formulation. It is the most complete variational MHD model in this family when both viscosity and resistivity are required.
normalizationHtml:
The model uses Alfvén-speed normalization together with entropy-based

thermodynamic units inherited from the chosen internal-energy functional.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.variational_density_evolve.VariationalDensityEvolve
  2. struphy.propagators.variational_momentum_advection.VariationalMomentumAdvection
  3. struphy.propagators.variational_entropy_evolve.VariationalEntropyEvolve
  4. struphy.propagators.variational_mag_field_evolve.VariationalMagFieldEvolve
  5. struphy.propagators.variational_viscosity.VariationalViscosity (if with_viscosity is True)
  6. struphy.propagators.variational_resistivity.VariationalResistivity (if with_resistivity is True)
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Kinetic energy: en_U
  • Thermodynamic energy: en_thermo
  • Magnetic energy: en_mag
  • Total energy: en_tot
  • Total density / entropy: dens_tot, entr_tot
  • Divergence diagnostic: tot_div_B
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • nonlinear dissipative MHD simulations
  • entropy-based variational MHD benchmarks
  • studies where both viscosity and resistivity matter
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • ideal nondissipative MHD if strict conservation is required
  • kinetic or hybrid particle effects
  • reduced linear perturbation studies better served by the linear models

name: ViscousEulerSPH
description: Euler equations with viscosity discretized with smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH).
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

ρ (∂ₜ 𝐮 + 𝐮 · ∇ 𝐮) = -∇ ( ρ² ∂𝒰(ρ, S)∂ρ ) - ∇ · π

Entropy:

∂ₜ S + 𝐮 · ∇ S = 0

where S denotes the entropy per unit mass and π is the viscous stress tensor.

The viscous stress tensor for a Newtonian fluid is given by:

σ = -μ ( ∇ 𝐮 + (∇ 𝐮)ᵀ - 23 (∇ · 𝐮) 𝐈 )

where μ is the dynamic (shear) viscosity and 𝐈 is the identity tensor.

The internal energy per unit mass can be defined in two ways:

isothermal:    𝒰(ρ, S) = κ(S) \log ρ

polytropic:    𝒰(ρ, S) = κ(S) ργ - 1γ - 1
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscousEulerSPH is the particle-based SPH fluid model with optional

pressure and viscosity contributions. It is intended for meshfree fluid experiments rather than FEEC-based field simulations.
normalizationHtml:
The characteristic speed is thermal:

û = \hat vₜₕ.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_eta.PushEta
  2. struphy.propagators.push_vxb.PushVxB (if with_B0 is True)
  3. struphy.propagators.push_vin_sph_pressure.PushVinSPHpressure (if with_p is True)
  4. struphy.propagators.push_vin_viscous_potential.PushVinViscousPotential (if with_viscosity is True)
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • SPH kinetic energy: en_kin
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • SPH verification with pressure and viscosity
  • meshfree compressible-fluid experiments
  • testing particle-based viscosity and pressure pushers
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • FEEC grid-based fluid or MHD formulations
  • entropy-resolved thermodynamic evolution
  • kinetic plasma physics
  • studies that require exact field-based conservation structures
examplesHtml:

from struphy.models import ViscousEulerSPH

model.euler_fluid.var

name: DeterministicParticleDiffusion
description: Diffusion equation discretized with a deterministic particle method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Find u : ℝ × Ω → ℝ⁺ such that

∂u∂t + ∇ · ( 𝐅(u) u ) = 0,    𝐅(u) = -𝔻 ∇ uu

where 𝔻 : Ω → ℝ3 × 3 is a positive diffusion matrix. At the moment only matrices of the form D * Id are implemented, where D > 0 is a positive diffusion coefficient.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a particle discretization of diffusion where particles follow a

deterministic drift derived from the current estimate of the density. It is intended mainly for diffusion-method development and verification rather than plasma dynamics.
normalizationHtml:
The diffusion coefficient defines the normalization,

D̂ = x̂² / t̂.

No separate plasma velocity scale is used in this model.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_deterministic_diffusion.PushDeterministicDiffusion
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • No default scalar diagnostics are defined by this model.
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • deterministic particle discretizations of diffusion
  • transport benchmarks with positive scalar densities
  • numerical comparison against stochastic diffusion methods
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • electromagnetic plasma dynamics
  • kinetic Vlasov problems in phase space
  • nonlinear fluid systems with pressure or momentum evolution
  • diffusion tensors outside the currently supported simplified forms

name: DriftKineticElectrostaticAdiabatic
description: Electrostatic drift-kinetic model for a single ion species with adiabatic electrons.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Drift-kinetic equation:

∂f∂t + [ v∥ 𝐁*B*∥ + 𝐄* × 𝐛₀B*∥ ] · ∂f∂𝐗 + [ 1ε 𝐁*B*∥ · 𝐄* ] · ∂f∂v∥ = 0

Poisson equation:

-∇⟂ · ( n₀|B₀|² ∇⟂ φ ) + 1ε n₀ ( 1 + 1Z ε 1T₀ φ ) = 1ε ∫ f B*∥   d v∥ d μ

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄* = -∇ φ - ε μ ∇ |B₀|,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀

The control variate method can be activated in the Poisson equation; if enabled, the following Poisson equation is solved:

-∇⟂ · ( n₀|B₀|² ∇⟂ φ ) + 1Z ε² n₀T₀ φ = 1ε ∫ (f - f₀) B*∥   d v∥ d μ
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is an electrostatic drift-kinetic reduction for strongly

magnetized ions in a fixed magnetic equilibrium. Electrons are not evolved kinetically; instead they enter through the adiabatic response in the quasi-neutrality solve. The implementation supports control variates for the field solve.
normalizationHtml:
The reference speed is the ion thermal speed and the electrostatic

fields are scaled accordingly:

v̂ = \hat vᵢ,   Ê = \hat vᵢ B̂,   \hatφ = Ê x̂.

The small parameter is ε = 1/(\hatΩct̂).
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.implicit_diffusion.ImplicitDiffusion
  2. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_bx_estar.PushGuidingCenterBxEstar
  3. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_parallel.PushGuidingCenterParallel
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Field energy: en_phi
  • Guiding-center particle energy: en_particles
  • Total energy: en_tot
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • electrostatic drift-kinetic ion turbulence studies
  • strongly magnetized plasmas with adiabatic electrons
  • guiding-center PIC verification in realistic magnetic geometry
  • low-frequency regimes where full gyrophase resolution is unnecessary
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • fully electromagnetic dynamics with evolving magnetic perturbations
  • electron kinetic effects beyond the adiabatic closure

name: GuidingCenter
description: Guiding-center equation for a single species in a static background magnetic field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Guiding-center Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + [ v∥ 𝐁*B*∥ + 𝐄* × 𝐛₀B*∥ ] · ∂f∂𝐗 + [ 1ε 𝐁*B*∥ · 𝐄* ] · ∂f∂v∥ = 0

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄* = -ε μ ∇ |B₀|,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀
longDescriptionHtml:
GuidingCenter is the reduced kinetic model used when fast gyromotion is

averaged out and only guiding-center motion needs to be resolved. It evolves particles in a fixed magnetic background without any self-consistent field solve.
normalizationHtml:
The reference speed is Alfvénic and the key small parameter is the

normalized cyclotron time:

v̂ = \hat vA,   ε = 1/(\hatΩc t̂).
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_bx_estar.PushGuidingCenterBxEstar
  2. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_parallel.PushGuidingCenterParallel
scalarQuantitiesHtml:

  • Magnetic-moment energy contribution: en_fB
  • Total particle energy: en_tot
  • Lost markers: n_lost_particles
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • test-particle guiding-center orbit calculations
  • strongly magnetized plasmas with scale separation from gyromotion
  • verification of 5D guiding-center pushers and diagnostics
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • self-consistent electric or magnetic field evolution
  • full-orbit particle dynamics with resolved gyrophase
  • collisional transport or source terms not present in the equation
  • fluid closures or MHD force balance

name: LinearVlasovAmpereOneSpecies
description: Linearized Vlasov-Ampère equations for one kinetic species around a Maxwellian background.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Linearized Ampère's law:

∂Ẽ∂t = -α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f̃   d³ 𝐯

Linearized Vlasov equation:

∂f̃∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f̃ + 1ε ( 𝐄₀ + 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f̃∂𝐯 = 1vₜₕ² ε Ẽ · 𝐯 f₀

where Z=-1 and A=1/1836 for electrons. The background distribution function f₀ is a uniform Maxwellian

f₀ = n₀(𝐱)( √(2 π) vₜₕ )³ \exp ( - |𝐯|²2 vₜₕ² )

and the background electric field has to verify the following compatibility condition between with background density

∇𝐱 \ln (n₀(𝐱)) = 1vₜₕ² ε 𝐄₀

At initial time the weak Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy Gauss' law,

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱
=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   f̃   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱
∀ ψ ∈ H¹
Ẽ(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)

Moreover, it is assumed that

∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f₀   d³ 𝐯 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearVlasovAmpereOneSpecies is the linearized delta-f counterpart of

VlasovAmpereOneSpecies. It is intended for weakly perturbed kinetic problems around a prescribed Maxwellian equilibrium and is especially useful for linear instability or damping studies.
normalizationHtml:
The light speed defines the velocity scale:

v̂ = c,   Ê = B̂ v̂,   \hatφ = Ê x̂.

The species parameters are α=\hatΩₚ/\hatΩc and ε=1/(\hatΩct̂).
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_eta.PushEta
  2. struphy.propagators.push_vin_efield.PushVinEfield (if with_E0 is True)
  3. struphy.propagators.efield_weights_coupling.EfieldWeightsCoupling
  4. struphy.propagators.push_vxb.PushVxB (if with_B0 is True)

  • Electric field energy: en_E
  • Perturbation particle energy: en_w
  • Total energy: en_tot
useCasesHtml:

  • linear delta-f kinetic instabilities
  • weakly perturbed Landau-like damping studies with electrostatic fields
  • verification of linearized field-particle coupling
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • strongly nonlinear departures from the chosen equilibrium
  • multi-species kinetic coupling
  • fully electromagnetic magnetic-field evolution
  • equilibria that are not compatible with the built-in Maxwellian assumptions

longDescriptionHtml:

name: VlasovAmpereOneSpecies
description: Vlasov-Ampère system for a single kinetic species in an electric field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + 1ε ( 𝐄 + 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯

Initial Poisson equation: At t=0, solve weakly for the electric potential φ:

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   (f - f₀)   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱    ∀ ψ ∈ H¹
𝐄(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)
longDescriptionHtml:
This model couples the kinetic Vlasov equation for the particle distribution function

with Ampère's law for the electric field evolution. It includes the effect of a static background magnetic field 𝐁₀ and solves the initial Poisson equation to satisfy Gauss's law at t=0. The model uses a particle-in-cell (PIC) method with finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) for the electromagnetic fields.

All field variables are perturbations around a reference equilibrium distribution. The model enables studies of kinetic instabilities, particle-wave interactions, and nonlinear plasma physics without assuming a fluid approximation.
normalizationHtml:
Velocity and field normalizations:

v̂ = c,    Ê = B̂ v̂,    φ̂ = Ê x̂

Dimensionless parameters:

α = ω̂ₚω̂c,    ε = 1ω̂c t̂

where

ω̂ₚ = √(n̂ (Ze)²ε₀ (A mH)),    ω̂c = (Ze) B̂(A mH)

For electrons: Z = -1, A = 1/1836.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_eta.PushEta
  2. struphy.propagators.push_vxb.PushVxB (if with_B0 is True)
  3. struphy.propagators.vlasov_ampere_coupling.VlasovAmpereCoupling
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Electric field energy: EE = 1⁄2 ∫ |𝐄|²   dV
  • Kinetic energy: Ef = α²⁄2N ∑ₚ wₚ |𝐯ₚ|²
  • Total energy: Eₜₒₜ = EE + Ef
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • studying kinetic instabilities in collisionless plasmas
  • particle-wave interactions and nonlinear plasma physics
  • initial value problems with prescribed equilibrium distributions
  • benchmark problems for kinetic-field coupling schemes
  • verification of PIC methods in simplified geometries
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • multi-species systems (requires extension)
  • collision operator effects
  • electromagnetic wave propagation (no magnetic field evolution)
  • drift-reduced or gyrokinetic approximations (full 6D Vlasov equation)

pdeHtml:

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

𝐄(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)

Moreover, it is assumed that

∇ × 𝐁₀ = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f₀   d³ 𝐯

where 𝐁₀ is the static equilibrium magnetic field.
longDescriptionHtml:
VlasovMaxwellOneSpecies is the fully electromagnetic one-species PIC

model in Struphy. It evolves particles and fields self-consistently and supports an optional control-variate formulation for the field coupling.
normalizationHtml:
The model uses the light speed as reference velocity:

v̂ = c,   Ê = B̂ v̂,   \hatφ = Ê x̂.

discretizationHtml:

f₀ = n₀(𝐱)( √(2 π) vₜₕ )³ \exp ( - |𝐯|²2 vₜₕ² )

name: ColdPlasmaVlasov
description: Hybrid cold-plasma model: a cold electron fluid coupled with a hot kinetic species and Maxwell's equations.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Hot Vlasov species:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + 1εₕ \Big[ 𝐄 + 𝐯 × ( 𝐁 + 𝐁₀ ) \Big] · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0

Cold-plasma current:

1n₀ ∂𝐣c∂t = 1εc 𝐄 + 1εc n₀ 𝐣c × 𝐁₀

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²εₕ ( 𝐣c + ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯 )

where (n₀, 𝐁₀) denotes an inhomogeneous background.

At initial time the Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy the Gauss law:

∇ · 𝐄 = ν α²εₕ ∫ℝ³ f   d³ 𝐯
longDescriptionHtml:
ColdPlasmaVlasov is an electromagnetic hybrid model that keeps a cold

fluid response for the thermal electrons and a kinetic PIC description for a hot species. It is designed for problems where the energetic population matters kinetically but the bulk response can still be treated as cold.
normalizationHtml:
Velocities are normalized with the speed of light and the kinetic

background is scaled as

v̂ = c,   Ê = c B̂,   f̂ = n̂ / c³.

The model distinguishes cold and hot cyclotron scales through εc and εₕ.

name: LinearMHDDriftkineticCC
description: Hybrid linear ideal MHD coupled with energetic ions (5D drift-kinetic) via the current-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁 + (∇ × 𝐁₀) × B̃ + AₕAb [ 1ε ngc Ũ - 1ε 𝐉gc - ∇ × 𝐌gc ] × 𝐁

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁) = 0

Energetic-particle drift-kinetic equation:

∂fₕ∂t + 1B∥* ( v∥ 𝐁* - 𝐛₀ × 𝐄* ) · ∇ fₕ + 1ε 1B∥* (𝐁* · 𝐄*) ∂fₕ∂v∥ = 0

Energetic-particle moments:

ngc = ∫ fₕ B∥*   d v∥ d μ

𝐉gc = ∫ fₕB∥* ( v∥ 𝐁* - 𝐛₀ × 𝐄* )   d v∥ d μ

𝐌gc = -∫ fₕ B∥* μ 𝐛₀   d v∥ d μ

where

B*∥ = 𝐛₀ · 𝐁*
𝐁*=𝐁 + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀
𝐄*=-Ũ × 𝐁 - ε μ ∇ (𝐛₀ · 𝐁)
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDDriftkineticCC is the reduced-kinetic hybrid current-coupling

model for energetic ions. It is useful when gyrophase averaging is acceptable but energetic-particle feedback on linear MHD still has to be retained.
normalizationHtml:
The bulk and energetic-particle flow scales are normalized with the

bulk Alfvén speed, while the magnetic moment carries its own unit:

Û = v̂ = \hat vA,bulk,
\hatμ = Aₕ mH \hat vₕ² / B̂.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_bx_estar.PushGuidingCenterBxEstar
  2. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_parallel.PushGuidingCenterParallel
  3. struphy.propagators.current_coupling_5d_gradb.CurrentCoupling5DGradB
  4. struphy.propagators.current_coupling_5d_curlb.CurrentCoupling5DCurlb
  5. struphy.propagators.current_coupling_5d_density.CurrentCoupling5DDensity
  6. struphy.propagators.shear_alfven_current_coupling_5d.ShearAlfvenCurrentCoupling5D
  7. struphy.propagators.magnetosonic.Magnetosonic
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • MHD kinetic energy: en_U
  • Thermal pressure energy: en_p
  • Magnetic energy: en_B
  • Parallel energetic-particle energy: en_fv
  • Magnetic-moment energetic-particle energy: en_fB
  • Total energy: en_tot
  • Lost particles: n_lost_particles
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • linear energetic-ion effects with guiding-center reduction
  • current-coupling hybrid mode studies in strong magnetic fields
  • verification of 5D hybrid coupling operators
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • full 6D energetic-particle dynamics
  • nonlinear hybrid turbulence
  • resistive or viscous MHD closures
  • regimes where gyrophase resolution is required

name: LinearMHDVlasovCC
description: Hybrid linear MHD coupled with energetic ions (6D Vlasov) via the current-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + 𝐉₀ × B̃ \color{blue} + AₕAb 1ε ( nₕ Ũ - nₕ 𝐮ₕ ) × (𝐁₀ + B̃) \color{black}

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + (γ - 1) ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t = ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀),    ∇ · B̃ = 0

Energetic-particle Vlasov equation:

∂fₕ∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ fₕ + 1ε [ \color{blue} (𝐁₀ + B̃) × Ũ \color{black} + 𝐯 × (𝐁₀ + B̃) ] · ∂fₕ∂𝐯 = 0

Energetic-particle moments:

nₕ = ∫ℝ³ fₕ   d³ 𝐯,    nₕ 𝐮ₕ = ∫ℝ³ fₕ 𝐯   d³ 𝐯

where 𝐉₀ = ∇×𝐁₀.
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDVlasovCC is a current-coupling hybrid model for small

perturbations around an MHD equilibrium. It is intended for energetic particle effects on linear MHD waves and instabilities without the cost of a fully kinetic background plasma.
normalizationHtml:
Both fluid and particle velocities are normalized with the Alfvén

speed,

Û = v̂ = \hat vA,   \hat fₕ = n̂ / \hat vA³.

The hot-species cyclotron parameter is ε = 1/(\hatΩc,hott̂).

name: LinearMHDVlasovPC
description: Hybrid linear MHD coupled with energetic ions (6D Vlasov) via the pressure-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ + AₕAb ∇ · ℙ̃h,⟂ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + 𝐉₀ × B̃

𝐉₀ = ∇ × 𝐁₀

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0

Energetic-particle Vlasov equation:

∂fₕ∂t + (𝐯 + Ũ⟂) · ∇ fₕ + [ 1ε 𝐯 × (𝐁₀ + B̃) - ∇ Ũ⟂ · 𝐯 ] · ∂fₕ∂𝐯 = 0

Perpendicular pressure tensor:

ℙ̃h,⟂ = ∫ 𝐯⟂ 𝐯⟂ᵀ fₕ   d 𝐯
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDVlasovPC is the pressure-coupling counterpart to the

current-coupling hybrid model. It is targeted at linear problems where energetic-particle pressure anisotropy is the relevant feedback channel on the bulk MHD dynamics.
normalizationHtml:
Fluid and hot-particle velocities are normalized with the bulk Alfvén

speed. The kinetic pressure tensor is scaled consistently with Aₕ mH n̂ \hat vA², and the hot cyclotron parameter is ε.

name: Maxwell
description: Maxwell's equations in vacuum for electromagnetic field evolution.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Ampère's law (no current):

∂𝐄∂t - ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
This model simulates the propagation of electromagnetic waves in vacuum

using Maxwell's equations without sources. It uses a finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) formulation with the electric field in H(curl) and the magnetic field in H(div) spaces.
normalizationHtml:
Velocity and fields are normalized as:

v̂ = c ,   Ê = c B̂

where c is the speed of light.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.maxwell_weak_ampere.MaxwellWeakAmpere
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Electric energy: EE = 1⁄2 ∫ |𝐄|²   dV
  • Magnetic energy: EB = 1⁄2 ∫ |𝐁|²   dV
  • Total energy: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = EE + EB
useCasesHtml: Propagation of electromagnetic waves in vacuum.
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
Plasma dynamics, plasma-field interactions, or any scenario involving charged particles.

This model does not include any particle species or coupling to matter.
examplesHtml:
Create and initialize a Maxwell model: 

from struphy.models import Maxwell

model = Maxwell()
# Fields are accessible via:
model.em_fields.e_field
model.em_fields.b_field

name: ToyDrift
description: Electrostatic drift toy model for a single ion species in a given background magnetic field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Drift equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐄 × 𝐛₀B*∥ · ∂f∂𝐗 = 0

Poisson equation:

-∇ · ∇ φ = ∫ f B*∥   d v∥ d μ

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄 = -∇ φ,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀

The control variate method can be activated in the Poisson equation; if enabled, the following Poisson equation is solved:

-∇ · ∇ φ = ∫ (f - f₀) B*∥   d v∥ d μ
longDescriptionHtml:
ToyDrift is a stripped-down guiding-center model used to isolate the

electrostatic drift part of the dynamics. It is intended for algorithm prototyping and reduced verification problems rather than production drift-kinetic studies.
normalizationHtml:
The reference speed is the ion thermal velocity:

v̂ = \hat vᵢ,   Ê = \hat vᵢ B̂,   \hatφ = Ê x̂.
discretizationHtml:
Time integration is performed by the following propagators (in sequence):
  1. struphy.propagators.poisson_solve.PoissonSolve
  2. struphy.propagators.push_guiding_center_bx_estar.PushGuidingCenterBxEstar
scalarQuantitiesHtml:
The following scalars are tracked during simulation:

  • Electrostatic field energy: en_phi
  • Particle kinetic energy: en_particles
  • Total energy: en_tot
useCasesHtml:
This model is appropriate for:
  • reduced electrostatic guiding-center benchmarks
  • testing the field solve plus 𝐄×𝐁 pusher
  • algorithm prototyping before moving to the full drift-kinetic model
cannotBeUsedForHtml:
This model is not suitable for:
  • full drift-kinetic dynamics with parallel streaming
  • electromagnetic perturbations
  • high-fidelity turbulence studies
  • full-orbit kinetic physics
